description: PhotonX. Building a view of NASA SPHEREx sky data: enter any coordinate, step through observation epochs, and watch objects move between scans. Comets, asteroids, and Planet X candidates reveal themselves by shifting position. Looking for collaborators in frontend dev, data viz, or video production.
summary:
Hypothetical Planet Nine and cold brown dwarfs emit minimal visible light, making them undetectable by optical surveys. They do, however, emit faint thermal radiation in the infrared. NASA's SPHEREx mission is mapping the entire sky in 102 near-infrared spectral bands every six months, producing extensive time-series datasets.

PhotonX is an open-source web application designed to process and visualize this data. It provides an interactive multi-spectral sky engine, a 2D Keplerian Solar System Orrery, procedural planetary optics, and an automated pixel-differencing engine inspired by Clyde Tombaugh's optical comparator.

Users can extract 102-channel spectral profiles, isolate moving objects between survey epochs, evaluate local atmospheric seeing conditions, and export structured observation logs. The platform operates directly in standard web browsers with zero installation requirements, helping students, amateur astronomers, and researchers analyze real NASA infrared telemetry.
details:
What PhotonX Does & How It Works

PhotonX is an end-to-end astronomical discovery workstation that translates raw multi-epoch NASA space telescope telemetry into an accessible, interactive visual experience:

  1. Interactive Telescope Viewport & Procedural Optics: Renders celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) on a GPU-accelerated HTML5 Canvas with continuous coordinate projection and adaptive limiting magnitude (6.2 mv to 18.0 mv). Features high-resolution procedural renderers for major Solar System worlds—including Jupiter with cloud bands, Great Red Spot, and Galilean moons; 3D tilted ringed Saturn with Cassini division; Mars with polar ice caps; Venus; Earth and Moon; the Sun with granulation and sunspots; and deep-sky objects like Andromeda Galaxy (M31), Orion Nebula (M42), and Sagittarius A*.
  2. Interactive Keplerian Solar System Orrery: Real-time orbital mechanics simulating true Keplerian velocities across scale modes (Inner System 0–2 AU, Full System 0–40 AU, and Outer System / Planet Nine & Sedna up to 800 AU), complete with time controls (1x to 365x) and one-click telescope slew integration.
  3. Clyde Tombaugh Temporal Blink Engine: Recreates the classic discovery technique that found Pluto in 1930, cycling rapidly between 6-month SPHEREx survey cadence epochs (2025-W18, 2025-W44, 2026-W18, 2026-W44) to isolate high proper-motion movers and parallax displacement.
  4. 102-Band Spectrophotometric Profiler: Extracts calibrated 102-channel spectral energy distributions (0.75 to 5.00 µm) with diagnostic markers for biogenic ices (H2O, CO2, CO) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH).
  5. 3σ Pixel Differencing Engine: Computes flux variance matrices between survey epochs (Epoch B − Epoch A), clusters connected components above a tunable sigma threshold, and centroids moving object candidates.
  6. Ground-Based Atmospheric Seeing Engine: Evaluates optical observing conditions from any Earth coordinate (seeing disc in arcseconds, airmass via Pickering's formulation, and transparency) to guide follow-up telescope observations.
  7. Citizen Science "Hunt Mode": Gamified discovery workspace with ranking tiers (Infrared Tracker to Deep Space Pioneer) and instant export of NASA DOI-cited Markdown observation logs.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional astronomical software (IRAF, DS9, FITS viewers) requires heavy installation, command-line expertise, and massive local storage. PhotonX runs entirely inside a standard web browser with zero setup. It enables students, educators, amateur astronomers, and professional researchers worldwide to explore real NASA infrared data, participate in citizen science, and inspect potential Planet Nine candidates without technical barriers.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend: React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand state management, TanStack React Query, Lucide Icons, and HTML5 Canvas API (sub-pixel procedural rendering).
  • Backend & Astrophysics API: Python 3.12+, FastAPI, NumPy (matrix differencing and flux calculations), Astropy (WCS and celestial coordinates), HTTPX (asynchronous NASA API communications).
  • Client-Side Simulation Engine: Fully independent fallback calculation pipeline enabling the application to run as a zero-backend static progressive web application on GitHub Pages.
  • Hardware Requirements: Runs seamlessly on any modern desktop, laptop, or tablet browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) without discrete GPU requirements.

Creativity & Design Philosophy

PhotonX avoids generic dark dashboard templates in favor of a specialized Sand & Ocean design language inspired by desert launch complexes and deep space ocean worlds. It bridges 1930s astronomical history (Tombaugh's optical blink comparator) with modern multi-wavelength infrared astrophysics and live space weather telemetry.

Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Zero-Barrier Access: No user accounts, passwords, or installations required.
  • Scientific Authenticity: Uses real NASA SPHEREx calibration standards, filter passbands, and real-time NASA Open APIs.
  • Offline & Low-Bandwidth Resilience: Optimized client-side caching ensures the engine runs smoothly even under intermittent internet connections.
